title: Integrative AOP-Based Mechanistic Profiling of Organic UV Filters Reveals Shared Endocrine-Metabolic and Stress-Response Pathways.
authors: Accardi, Cristina; Al-Abdulraheem, Zeyad; Schaffert, Alexandra; Federico, Antonio; Del Giudice, Giusy; Serra, Angela; Greco, Dario
one_liner_zh: 该文基于AOP框架整合转录因子下游靶基因与分子对接预测蛋白靶点，剖析有机UV滤光剂的毒理机制，虽涉及TF-DNA调控网络和分子对接，但核心是毒理学通路分析而非TF-DNA结合互作机制建模，方法可迁移性有限。
abstract: Organic UV filters are widely used in personal care products and are increasingly detected in humans and the environment. Although several compounds exhibit systemic absorption and biological activity, their mechanisms of action remain poorly understood because comprehensive toxicogenomic data remain limited. Here, we developed an integrative Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP)-based framework to support the mechanistic profiling of organic UV filters with sparse experimental evidence. Molecular evidence was integrated from experimentally supported bioassay target genes, transcription factor downstream target genes derived from a curated regulatory network, and predicted protein targets obtained through molecular docking using GalaxySagittarius-AF. Docking-derived targets were prioritized using prediction scores and refined according to protein-protein interaction network proximity to bioassay-confirmed targets. Chemical-specific gene sets were tested for enrichment against curated human Key Event gene sets and mapped onto the AOP network. ADMET descriptors and GTEx tissue-expression data were incorporated to assess skin absorption relevance and tissue-specific biological plausibility. Ten organic UV filters met the skin absorption criteria and underwent mechanistic analysis. Integrated evidence revealed recurring molecular signatures involving nuclear receptor signalling, lipid metabolism, oxidative stress, inflammation, and DNA damage responses. AOP mapping highlighted convergence on endocrine-metabolic key events, including androgen and estrogen receptor signalling, PPAR-mediated lipid regulation, and hepatobiliary nuclear receptor pathways. Additional subnetworks linked oxidative and inflammatory processes with AOP regions associated with liver, breast, and neurotoxicity, representing mechanistic enrichment rather than evidence of causality. This framework enables mechanistic profiling despite limited toxicogenomic data, identifies biologically plausible pathways and shared molecular domains across structurally diverse UV filters, and provides a foundation for hypothesis generation and prioritization of future experimental studies.
abstract_zh: 有机紫外线吸收剂广泛用于个人护理产品中，并越来越多地在人类和环境中被检测到。尽管若干化合物表现出全身吸收和生物活性，但由于全面的毒理基因组学数据仍然有限，其作用机制仍知之甚少。在此，我们开发了一个基于整合性不良结局通路（Adverse Outcome Pathway, AOP）的框架，以支持对实验证据稀疏的有机紫外线吸收剂进行机制剖析。分子证据整合自实验支持的生物测定靶基因、源自精选调控网络的转录因子下游靶基因，以及通过使用GalaxySagittarius-AF进行分子对接获得的预测蛋白质靶标。对接衍生的靶标根据预测分数进行优先级排序，并根据与生物测定确认靶标的蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用网络邻近性进行细化。化学特异性基因集针对精选的人类关键事件基因集进行富集测试，并映射到AOP网络上。ADMET描述符和GTEx组织表达数据被纳入，以评估皮肤吸收相关性和组织特异性生物学合理性。十种有机紫外线吸收剂满足皮肤吸收标准并进行了机制分析。整合证据揭示了涉及核受体信号传导、脂质代谢、氧化应激、炎症和DNA损伤反应的重复分子特征。AOP映射突出了内分泌-代谢关键事件的汇聚，包括雄激素和雌激素受体信号传导、PPAR介导的脂质调节以及肝胆核受体通路。额外的子网络将氧化和炎症过程与与肝脏、乳腺和神经毒性相关的AOP区域联系起来，这代表了机制富集而非因果证据。该框架能够在毒理基因组学数据有限的情况下实现机制剖析，识别跨结构多样的紫外线吸收剂的生物学合理通路和共享分子域，并为假设生成和未来实验研究的优先级排序提供基础。
